subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept backup excludes only after explicit opt-in and per-asset semantics, or is the warning-based `.backupignore` and external-asset behavior acceptable for a first merge?
rationale: This changes backup safety and user expectations, and automation cannot choose whether implicit local exclude files and warning-only external-asset gaps are an acceptable product contract.

options.title: Require explicit complete semantics
options.body: Make `.backupignore` opt-in, apply patterns to every backed-up asset root, and preserve gitignore rule order before merge.

options.title: Accept warning-based first version
options.body: Land a narrower version with explicit maintainer approval that documents `.backupignore` auto-load and external-asset bypasses as known limitations.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: Close or pause this branch if maintainers want a smaller replacement PR based on current main's backup hardening.

recommendation.title: Require explicit complete semantics
recommendation.body: Make `.backupignore` opt-in, apply patterns to every backed-up asset root, and preserve gitignore rule order before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup hardening merger and backup test contributor with enough area context to choose the product contract.
